fluff.overview: Sungdong-STX Shipbuilding, a Terra-based firm with centuries of experience constructing fast-hulled surface vessels, designed the Moray Heavy Attack Submarine in 2635 for the Star League Defense Force. Contracted to provide the SLDF's Royal CAAN regiments with a heavily armed undersea fire support platform, Sungdong-STX drew on its expertise in submersible cargo vessel construction to create a formidable 140-ton submarine. The Moray was designed to operate in partnership with the lighter Manta Fast Attack Submarine, providing the heavy firepower and durability that its companion lacked. The pairing gave CAAN regiments a flexible undersea combat team capable of responding to threats across multi-hundred-kilometer engagement zones. The Moray earned a reputation as one of the most formidable conventional submarines in the Inner Sphere, capable of engaging targets ranging from enemy submersibles to surface vessels.
fluff.capabilities:
The Moray was built to absorb punishment and deliver devastating torpedo salvos. Its Electro-Motive 390 XL fusion engine provides a maximum flank speed of 54 kilometers per hour, considerably slower than the Manta but adequate for a vessel designed to hold position and fight rather than conduct hit-and-run attacks. The engine consumes nearly a quarter of the submarine's 140-ton displacement, a significant investment that provides extended mission duration and reliable power for the vessel's extensive weapons suite.

Eighteen tons of AquaTec ArmorSlab ferro-fibrous armor give the Moray exceptional survivability for a submarine of its class. CASE protection prevents ammunition detonations from destroying the vessel outright, a critical feature given the large torpedo magazines carried aboard. The hull provides comprehensive coverage across all aspects, allowing the Moray to endure sustained engagements that would quickly overwhelm lighter submarines.

The weapons fit is extensive and well-distributed. The bow mounts twin Sea Devastator twenty-tube long-range torpedo launchers alongside a Sea Harvester six-tube short-range torpedo launcher. A dorsal turret carries an additional ten-tube long-range torpedo launcher, a short-range torpedo launcher, and a pair of Averell Poseidon extended-range medium lasers. Stern-mounted launchers eliminate blind spots in the engagement envelope. Three tons of ammunition per long-range launcher type and four tons for the short-range systems provide reasonable endurance for extended patrols, though the Moray's ammunition dependency remains its primary operational constraint.
fluff.deployment: The standard Moray represents the Word of Blake's updated configuration introduced in 3072, incorporating extended-range medium lasers in place of the original standard models. This version remains in active production and service with the Republic of the Sphere. Republic forces deploy the Moray primarily in its traditional role as the heavy anchor of submarine task forces, providing fire support for lighter Manta escorts. The type also serves independently in defense of underwater installations and as a mobile torpedo platform for coastal interdiction operations.
fluff.history:
Sungdong-STX Shipbuilding developed the Moray in 2635 as the heavy partner to the planned Manta fast attack submarine. At the height of the twenty-eighth century, Sungdong-STX operated facilities across a dozen Hegemony worlds producing submersibles ranging from bulk cargo vessels to underwater aerospace carriers. The Moray represented the firm's response to an SLDF requirement for a heavily armored support submarine capable of anchoring undersea combat teams in contested waters.

The Moray served with distinction in CAAN regiments throughout the Terran Hegemony. During the Amaris Civil War, Moray crews fought in defense of Terra's oceans, though the conflict exacted a heavy toll on the submarine fleet. The Succession Wars proved fatal to the design's continued service. Advanced components required for the extra-light engine and ferro-fibrous armor became irreplaceable as the technological base of the Inner Sphere collapsed, and the last operational examples were decommissioned by ComStar after it assumed control of Terra.

The Word of Blake's seizure of Terra brought the Moray back from extinction. Sungdong-STX's production lines were reactivated alongside Royal Nelson's Manta facility as part of the Blakist program to field Wyrm SDS Submersible Fortresses. New Morays entered service as escorts for these massive underwater weapons platforms, operating in their traditional paired role with newly built Mantas. The Blakists upgraded the original laser armament to extended-range models during reactivation, the only meaningful change to the decades-old configuration.

After Terra's liberation in 3079, surviving Morays joined the Coalition effort to neutralize rogue Wyrm platforms still under Blakist control. The Republic of the Sphere retained both the design and Sungdong-STX's production capability, continuing to build new hulls to support underwater command infrastructure and the remaining Wyrm fortresses under Republic authority.
